title: 2026 MLB Regular-Season Grades: ESPN Ranks All 30 Teams in Full Final Report
body:
The 2026 Major League Baseball regular season has drawn to a close, and ESPN’s final grade cards reveal a landscape of triumphs, disappointments and a few surprises that will shape the offseason narrative. The Los Angeles Dodgers, once again a juggernaut, flirted with the single‑season win record, while the New York Mets’ dramatic resurgence earned them a top‑tier grade. Conversely, perennial contenders such as the Houston Astros and the Boston Red Sox fell short of expectations, receiving middling to poor assessments that will likely trigger roster overhauls and strategic pivots. Every franchise now faces a clear verdict: the teams that earned high marks are poised for a deep postseason run, while those with low scores must confront the reality of rebuilding.

The Dodgers finished the year with a staggering 108 victories, just two wins shy of the all‑time mark set by the 1906 Chicago Cubs. Their offensive juggernaut—anchored by Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and a breakout rookie slugger—combined with a rotation that boasted a sub‑3.00 ERA on average. The grading committee rewarded the Dodgers with an A‑, citing their consistency, depth and ability to maintain elite performance despite mid‑season injuries. Their front office’s blend of veteran contracts and shrewd trades has positioned them as the team most likely to clinch a World Series berth, assuming they can translate regular‑season dominance into postseason resilience.

New York’s Mets, long considered a rebuilding project, earned a solid B+ after an unexpected surge that vaulted them into the National League East race. A revitalized pitching staff, highlighted by a 2.68 ERA from veteran ace Jacob deGrom and a breakout season from rookie left‑hander Luis García, complemented a potent middle‑lineup that posted the league’s second‑best on‑base percentage. The Mets’ grade reflects both the upside of their young core and the lingering questions surrounding their bullpen reliability, a factor that could prove decisive in October. Nevertheless, the Mets’ performance has injected optimism into a fan base that has endured years of mediocrity.

Not all stories were uplifting. The Houston Astros, despite fielding a lineup that led the league in slugging, slipped to a disappointing 84‑78 record, earning a C‑ grade. Injuries to key players and an underperforming bullpen undermined their otherwise potent offense. The grading panel highlighted the Astros’ failure to adapt mid‑season, pointing to a lack of strategic flexibility that left them trailing in the fiercely competitive AL West. Similarly, the Boston Red Sox received a D+ after a dismal 73‑89 finish, plagued by an anemic offense and a rotation that posted a collective ERA above 5.00. Their grade underscores a franchise in disarray, with rumors already swirling about managerial changes and a possible front‑office shake‑up.

Mid‑market clubs displayed a range of outcomes that could reshape the league’s power balance. The Seattle Mariners, long‑overlooked, earned a B after posting a 93‑69 record and securing a wild‑card spot, thanks to a balanced attack and a bullpen that posted the league’s best save conversion rate. The Chicago Cubs, on the other hand, received a C+ after a roller‑coaster season that saw them hover around .500 before a late‑season collapse cost them a playoff berth. Their grade reflects both the promise of a youthful core and the need for veteran leadership to steady the ship.

Looking ahead, the grades serve as a roadmap for the offseason. Teams with high marks, like the Dodgers and Mets, are expected to reinforce their strengths—adding depth to bullpens and shoring up defensive versatility—to ensure they can navigate the pressures of October. Conversely, low‑graded clubs will likely enter the trade market aggressively, targeting proven arms and power hitters to close the gaps exposed this year. As free agency looms and the draft approaches, the narrative set by these evaluations will influence every contract negotiation and roster decision, setting the stage for a 2027 season that promises to be as unpredictable as the grades themselves.
